intent: Create one fixed-scene 2x2 matrix that teaches the difference between focal perspective and physical camera distance without reusing family identity artwork.
fixedScene: One synthetic adult presenting the same small cobalt product case in the same pale concrete courtyard; eye-height camera; neutral wardrobe; clean soft daylight; 4:3 landscape; same subject identity, pose, camera height, light, background geometry, output canvas, and product across all four cells. Distance-driven framing and scale consequences remain observable.
creativeDirection: Keep the courtyard broad enough to judge near/far scale. The 24mm-neutral cell opens the environment; the 24mm-close cell makes the near case or hands visibly larger; the 35mm-neutral cell is calmer; the 35mm-close cell adds restrained dimensional scale. Treat the four cells as one controlled study, not four unrelated hero images, and do not erase the distance effect with compensating crops or digital rescaling.
requiredCues: 24mm-neutral is wider than 35mm-neutral without fisheye curvature
24mm-close shows the strongest near-feature scale relative to background
35mm-close shows a restrained but visible near-feature scale increase
both close cells read as camera-distance changes rather than crop-only changes
near-feature and background-scale differences repeat across reruns
avoidCues: gratuitous crop, digital rescale, or compensating crop that erases the distance effect
changed camera height, pose, light, scene geometry, or product
digital zoom or background blur as the only difference
comparisonTolerance: Compare stable scene and subject identity; allow distance-driven subject/background scale and framing changes. Promotion requires repeatable near-feature/background-scale separation across reruns.

intent: Show a clean three-quarter viewpoint as a horizontal camera relationship, with the front and side planes both readable.
fixedScene: The same synthetic adult and cobalt product case in a pale concrete courtyard; 50mm-class cue; eye-height camera; soft daylight; neutral palette; 4:3 landscape; stable subject placement and crop.
creativeDirection: Use a quiet, diagram-like portrait scene with one subject turned enough to reveal front and side planes. Let the camera relationship carry the example; do not add fashion styling, dramatic light, or a hero crop that could be mistaken for the angle.
requiredCues: front and side planes are both visible
diagonal relationship is clear but readable
subject and product remain in the same place
avoidCues: decorative family object or text overlay

intent: Show subject hierarchy: one unmistakable hero subject with a subordinate environment.
fixedScene: A synthetic runner in a plain cobalt jacket presents a small cobalt product case in a quiet concrete courtyard; 35mm-class cue; clean three-quarter view; soft daylight; 4:3 landscape.
creativeDirection: Build a strong silhouette and a calm field around the runner. The case and runner should read as one hero story, while the courtyard supports scale and context without becoming a competing subject. Judge hierarchy and environmental subordination only; do not use campaign styling as an acceptance cue.
requiredCues: product remains readable without becoming a second equal focal point
avoidCues: repeated lens, stage, or finish family object

intent: Show a bright high-key soft key through exposure, open shadows, and controlled highlights rather than through a generic studio prop.
fixedScene: A synthetic cobalt cosmetic bottle on a matte white plinth in a pale studio; 50mm-class cue; centered product hierarchy; neutral background; 4:3 landscape.
creativeDirection: Make the light legible on the bottle's curved surface and the plinth. The image should feel bright and clean while retaining enough shadow to prove softness and form; the setup itself should stay visually quiet. This illustrates the accepted high-soft compound seed and does not validate a pure light.key decomposition.
requiredCues: product silhouette and label area remain readable
avoidCues: stage-family asset used as a lighting example

intent: Show a clean white-blue palette as a finish direction that can be changed without silently changing the light source or composition.
fixedScene: A synthetic person in a neutral outfit sits at a minimal modern desk; eye-level 50mm-class cue; three-quarter composition; soft daylight from camera-left; 4:3 landscape; neutral white balance held constant.
creativeDirection: Use bright white surfaces and controlled clean-blue accents in the architecture, materials, and objects. Lock neutral white balance and the same daylight direction so the example teaches palette through surfaces, wardrobe, and architecture rather than a blue-tinted light or a cyberpunk mood.
requiredCues: controlled clean-blue accents in materials or architecture
neutral white balance under the same fixed light
avoidCues: finish-family raster used as the example

intent: Show the commercial seed as a deconstructible six-part recipe rather than as an opaque branded look.
fixedScene: A synthetic adult presents a small cobalt product case in a controlled pale studio set; 35mm-class environmental cue; clean three-quarter view; hero hierarchy; high-key soft light; medium depth with a legible background; 4:3 landscape.
creativeDirection: The image should read first as a polished commercial hero, then reveal its parts: natural perspective, three-quarter relationship, subject hierarchy, high-key softness, restrained commercial finish, and a background that remains legible. Keep the studio set plain enough that no hidden style direction is doing the work.
requiredCues: all six seed directions are visible together
natural perspective rather than extreme distortion
legible background without competing focal points
avoidCues: family identity artwork presented as a practical example
